baseline_format_facts: The baseline writer emits canonical epoch:branch identifiers such as8:tech, using decimal integer formatting without padding.
The baseline loader validates Integer.parseInt(epoch) but retains the original proof string. Consequently08:tech and+8:tech can pass parsing yet do not satisfy a query for8:tech.

Canonicalizing a noncanonical historical identifier would change authorization. A safe migration must retain its inert meaning or block the unsupported journal while preserving original bytes; it must not silently activate aliases.
clearRuntime resets live rules, eligibility and attempt caches. Genuine historical receipt data must survive runtime reset and full server restart.
installer_facts: Installer plan_install selects kubejs/,config/ and the single owned companion JAR. It does not enumerate worlds/saves or TeamData journals.

Existing config/ftbquests/quests/data.snbt is left unchanged, and old owned companion JARs are backed up before replacement. Journal hardening is a native read/write policy, not an installer world-save migration.
required_validation: Malformed or existing unreadable journals are preserved and cannot become empty writable data.
Reading/configuration/runtime cleanup cannot create new proofs.
Repeated true proof recording is idempotent even at capacity.
Full native NBT/restart and modeled IO tests must be reported separately from complete optional-mod/client acceptance.
binary_scope: Actual common NeoForge SDK source+compiled artifact; not evidence that optional Ad Astra/FTB/KubeJS binaries were launched.
